profile.reading: This OSM record, "Tahoe Reno 5," is mapped to Switch's "Citadel Campus" in the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County, Nevada, sharing the same 1 Superloop Circle address as the other numbered Tahoe Reno buildings in this dataset, but could not be confirmed as an individually named or specified Switch facility this session. Switch's own website, full press-release archive, and its FY2021 SEC 10-K filing, its last as a public company before the 2022 DigitalBridge/IFM take-private transaction, name and give specifications only for Tahoe Reno 1 (opened, 1.3 million-plus square feet, 130 megawatts) and, at a groundbreaking stage with no individual specs, Tahoe Reno 2 and 3; no Switch press release, SEC filing, or campus page found this session names a "Tahoe Reno 5" specifically. The FY2021 10-K discloses seven future facilities in aggregate (5.89 million square feet, 520 megawatts combined) without individually naming or numbering them, which likely explains why third-party mapping data assigns sequential "Tahoe Reno 4" and "Tahoe Reno 5" labels, since these appear to be placeholder or extrapolated labels applied by mapping or aggregator sources rather than confirmed Switch-published building names. This profile does not assert that a building called "Tahoe Reno 5" specifically exists as a distinct, confirmed structure separate from the campus's undifferentiated future-facility total, consistent with this dataset's practice of flagging genuine ambiguity rather than guessing. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at up to 17.4 million square feet and more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, roughly three times the megawatt figure and more than double the square footage Switch cited for the same campus as recently as 2021, reflecting a major post-acquisition re-scoping of the site's ambitions.

reading.body:
"Tahoe Reno 5" is not an individually named or specified facility in Switch's published materials or SEC filings; it appears to be a label applied by third-party mapping sources to one of seven future buildings in the Citadel Campus aggregate, described in Switch's FY2021 10-K with no individual building designations. Switch's current marketing describes the full Citadel Campus at more than 2 gigawatts of power at completion, roughly three times the megawatt figure the operator cited for the same campus in 2021, indicating major post-acquisition re-scoping. Because no individual specification for this building exists in the operator's published record, no capacity figure, efficiency rating, or grid-interconnection detail can be assigned to it as a distinct asset.

Switch has named and specified only Tahoe Reno 1 among the Nevada buildings at this address, disclosing it as operational at 130 megawatts across 1.3 million square feet. The Citadel Campus full build-out target of 650 megawatts is a multi-building figure that does not clarify how power will be distributed across individual future structures or when those structures will come online. Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities statewide, of which only 2 have published capacity figures totaling 10.37 megawatts, placing this campus third by published megawatts if Tahoe Reno 1's specification were applied, but the state grid's total committed capacity to data centers remains opaque.

Without individual specifications for Tahoe Reno 5, this profile cannot evaluate its material significance to AI infrastructure scaling or its constraint on grid capacity. A reader deciding whether this campus matters should track Switch's disclosure of individual building specifications and grid-interconnection agreements as they enter the public record, rather than rely on third-party extrapolation from aggregate campus figures.
